name: eval-sandbox-poisoned-metrics
repo_anchor: This host already runs the target pattern in miniature, outside the weco loop. MEMORY.md 2026-09-08 (recovery + prep): 'the probe driver gained abort-on-consecutive-failure and model/outdir args; preflight_window.sh encodes every environment failure the last window paid for (GPUs free, clocks, CUDA_HOME, flashinfer bypass, d256 kernel smoke on both model shapes - known-good control first)' - i.e. a K-consecutive-failure circuit breaker and a known-good canary already exist for the probe driver, not for weco evals. MEMORY.md 2026-09-08 (GPU window): 'the weco acceptance eval (23/23 entries oracle-clean under a unified fp64 gate, baseline 23.50 TFLOP/s at M512...)' - oracle-first catches wrong VALUES; nothing catches hangs or systematically-broken evals. The weco fork materialized at software/weco-skill/main (pin 707e1324, CLI weco 0.4.0 from connollydavid/weco-cli@0111f27e per .host-software): references/cli-reference.md documents '--eval-timeout | - | Timeout in seconds per evaluation' (default unset) for the cloud optimizer; references/local-mode.md documents the local loop ('weco local run --eval-command ... --metric ... --goal min|max --steps N') and its sandboxing ('systemd user container units (Quadlet) via the weco.local container driver, or a reproducible chroot'); a grep of all fork references finds zero occurrences of null/failure/retry semantics for eval outcomes; references/guidelines.md warns a stray 'correct: 0' comment 'would be parsed as a metric'; assets/evaluate-llm-judge.py returns a neutral 3.0 on judge-parse failure ('Return neutral score on parse failure') - the only null-adjacent policy in the fork, and it is continue-semantics. The local loop itself (weco-cli) evals via bash -c with no timeout and records value:null on unparseable metrics, continuing (per the lacuna statement; the CLI source is not materialized in this worktree, weco-skill is).
current_status: As of 2026-09-11 every surveyed domain independently converged on the same three-part answer at the eval boundary: a hard per-eval timeout, an explicit outcome taxonomy that separates 'candidate is bad' from 'eval is broken', and a breaker that stops the campaign when the eval itself is sick. Nobody mature runs continue-on-null silently. (1) SWE-BENCH HARNESS (github.com/SWE-bench/SWE-bench, swebench.com): one Docker container per instance; per-instance test timeout via --timeout, default 1800s (SWEBENCH_DOCKER_TIMEOUT env also defaults 1800); tests exec'd via exec_run_with_timeout(container, '/bin/bash /eval.sh', timeout) returning (test_output, timed_out, total_runtime); on timeout the harness appends 'Timeout error: N seconds exceeded' to the saved log, raises EvaluationError, run_instance catches it and returns None - no report.json is written, so the resume path (exclude_completed=True skips instances with existing report.json) re-runs exactly the unfinished ones; the batch itself never aborts (run_threadpool; per-instance exceptions are swallowed); container removed in finally. Integrity of the oracle: the harness test patch is applied over the model patch, so tests come from the harness, not the candidate; the PASS_TO_PASS suite must keep passing, acting as within-eval sentinels against both candidate regressions and harness rot (issue #437 'Make sure submitted patch doesn't modify tests'). The 2025-2026 integrity literature on gaming: Cursor's 'Reward Hacking is Swamping Model Intelligence Gains' (audit transcripts, constrain the eval environment); ImpossibleBench (hiding test files from the model drives hacking to near zero); UTBoost/Daniel Kang (test-coverage gaps let wrong patches pass); OpenAI's 'Why we no longer evaluate SWE-bench Verified' (contamination); arXiv 2507.05619 (empirical reward-hacking detection framework, 78.4% precision). (2) FUZZERS: libFuzzer (LLVM docs) ships -timeout (default 1200s; OSS-Fuzz runs 25-30s), -rss_limit_mb (default 2048), -malloc_limit_mb, and classifies every terminal input into distinct categories with separate artifacts - crash-*, timeout-*, oom-* - plus the 'ALARM: working on the last Unit for N seconds' hang alarm; ClusterFuzz reproduces and types every report (crash/OOM/timeout-hang) and embeds the engine settings line ('[libfuzzer] rss_limit_mb = 6000 timeout = 30') in each report, so eval-health parameters travel with every result. AFL++ uses per-exec -t, FAULT_TIMEOUT, and classifies hangs relative to the calibration average with AFL_HANG_TMOUT (default 1 second or the -t value [uncertain - sources state the relation both ways]); unique hangs are deduped by coverage and stored in hangs/ separately from crashes/, with first-class counters (saved_crashes, unique_hangs) in fuzzer_stats. The transferable core: crash/hang/OOM are three DIFFERENT recorded outcomes, never one 'failed', and hang detection is calibrated against observed execution-time distribution rather than a fixed guess. (3) CI SYSTEMS: GitHub Actions timeout-minutes defaults to 360 minutes - the canonical hung-job-burns-the-night failure, with 'always set an explicit per-job timeout' as standing doctrine; on cancel/timeout the runner signals SIGINT, waits 7.5s, SIGTERM, waits 2.5s, then force-kills, and only the TOP-LEVEL process gets signaled (documented orphaned-process-tree hazard - directly relevant to a bash -c that spawns GPU workers); matrix fail-fast auto-cancels siblings on first failure; flakiness is handled at test level with retry-and-mark (Bazel --flaky_test_attempts=N marks FLAKY and refuses to cache flaky results; pytest-rerunfailures). Service-engineering circuit breakers (Hystrix, Envoy outlier detection): common trip thresholds are 5 consecutive failures or 30-50% error rate over a sliding window. (4) AUTOML: Optuna 5.x - uncaught exceptions mark the trial FAIL and ABORT the study by default (fail-fast); catch=(Exception,) is the explicit opt-in to continue; NaN returns are FAIL but do not abort; heartbeat + RetryHeartbeatStaleTrialCallback detect and re-queue trials whose PROCESS died (hung/killed evals detected as stale-RUNNING). SMAC3 2.x - crash_cost (default np.inf) imputes crashed trials with a worst-case sentinel cost, recorded and marked crashed (fed to the run history; practitioners set it finite because inf disrupts the surrogate); abort_on_first_run_crash + FirstRunCrashedException abort if the FIRST/default config crashes - the default config doubles as a K=1 eval-health canary; historical issue #125 (first run crashes -> surrogate has zero data points) is the exact 'campaign burns as nulls' bug class. Google Vizier (KDD 2017; Vertex AI; oss-vizier) - Trial states ACTIVE/INFEASIBLE/SUCCEEDED/FAILED; 'Vizier supports marking trials as infeasible, in which case they do not receive an objective value' - a three-valued outcome where constraint-violation is not failure; practitioner guidance (Tripp 2024): map infeasible to a moderately negative value, never an extreme one. Ray Tune 2.x - trial states RUNNING/PAUSED/TERMINATED/ERROR with a per-trial error_file; TuneConfig(fail_fast=True)/FailureConfig stops the ENTIRE experiment when a trial errors (explicit circuit-breaker knob); legacy max_failures/raise_on_failed_trial. (5) THEORY: evolutionary dynamic optimization has run eval-drift canaries for two decades - 'detecting changes by re-evaluating solutions is by far the most common change-detection approach' (Nguyen, Nguyen & Yao survey 2012; detectors/sensors/sentries re-evaluated each generation; Jin & Branke 2005 for re-evaluation under uncertainty); reward-hacking/specification-gaming is catalogued (Krakovna's DeepMind list; Lilian Weng's 2024-11-28 overview; KL-vs-reward divergence as a runtime detector).
applicability: TRANSFERS DIRECTLY to the weco-local long-range runner: (a) Per-eval timeout with process-GROUP kill - the fork's cloud CLI already has --eval-timeout (seconds, default unset) but the local loop runs bash -c bare; the GHA lesson (only the top-level process is signaled; children keep the GPU) means the wrapper must killpg the session, not signal the shell; libFuzzer/AFL calibrate hang thresholds against the observed wall-clock distribution rather than a fixed guess, which matters here because eval cost varies with M/dtype. (b) Three-valued outcome per step: value | candidate-crash | infra-crash (timeout, unparseable output, missing metric line). The current value:null-and-continue collapses all three: an infra-broken eval is indistinguishable from a bad candidate AND from a boundary-value success, and a wall of nulls poisons the LLM mutator's context while burning window wall-clock. (c) Null semantics, per the surveyed consensus: candidate-crash = record a crash sentinel (metric-floor imputation, SMAC3-style, finite not infinite per the Vizier/Tripp lesson), keep the step logged, let the campaign continue - a candidate that OOMs is information; infra-crash = retry once immediately (Optuna RetryHeartbeatStaleTrialCallback pattern), and if the retry also fails, record NO value at all (never fabricate a number), increment the infra counter; breaker trips on 3 consecutive infra failures or >30% infra over a 10-step sliding window (Hystrix/Envoy numbers), halting with a distinct exit code so the overnight operator finds a diagnosis, not a .runs directory of nulls. Note the surveyed default is fail-fast or sentinel-impute, never silent-continue - Optuna aborts by default, SMAC imputes-and-marks, Vizier separates feasible/infeasible; weco local's continue-on-null is the outlier, and it is the failure mode, not a design choice to preserve. (d) Resume semantics: SWE-bench's no-report-on-failure contract (unfinished instances re-run, completed ones skipped by artifact presence) is the model for the runner's step ledger - cache only VALUE steps; non-value outcomes are never 'done'. (e) Eval-health as a first-class metric lane: re-evaluate the frozen baseline candidate every N steps and assert it inside its recorded band (EDO detectors; this host's own preflight 'known-good control first'); log null-rate, timeout-rate, eval wall-clock trend, and baseline-band drift into the same JSONL the campaign reads; PASS_TO_PASS analog: 2-3 fixed oracle entries (from the 23/23 fp64 gate) evaluated in EVERY run - any canary miss invalidates the step's value regardless of what the metric line said. (f) Poisoned-metric screens, in priority order: physical bounds (value must sit under the DRAM-derived floor/ceiling the runbook already carries), implausible-jump rule (a claimed new best beyond ~5x the historical band requires an oracle re-run before promotion to champion), constraint lines (weco already parses 'Constraint violated:'), and keeping the eval script + oracle data outside the optimizer's writable surface (ImpossibleBench/OpenAI lesson: what the mutator cannot read or edit, it cannot game; weco edits the candidate tree - the eval must live elsewhere). DOES NOT TRANSFER: Docker-per-instance isolation (SWE-bench) - the fork already documents Quadlet/chroot sandboxing and a single-user GPU host pays container overhead for little gain; the load-bearing gaps are timeout/classification/breaker, not isolation. OSS-Fuzz-scale crash dedup and triage infrastructure - overkill for one lane; the artifact-per-failure pattern (persist eval log + candidate snapshot on any non-value outcome) is the transferable core. Ray Tune's kill-experiment-on-first-trial-error applied to ALL failures - too aggressive for candidate crashes, which are ordinary optimization information; the breaker belongs on the infra-classified counter only.
mechanism: Implement the eval step as a state machine behind an exit-code contract, wrapper-level in the campaign runner. (1) WRAPPER: subprocess.run(['timeout', '--signal=TERM', '--kill-after=30s', str(T_max), 'bash', '-c', eval_cmd], start_new_session=True) so the whole process group dies; on exit 124/137 classify outcome 'timeout'; T_max = clamp(6 x median(last 5 successful eval wall-clocks), floor=600s, ceil=window-budget/remaining-steps) - AFL-style calibration against the observed distribution, recomputed as the campaign matures. (2) OUTCOME CONTRACT per step, written to a step ledger JSONL: outcome_class in {value, candidate_crash, timeout, infra_crash}; rules - exit 0 AND metric line parsed -> value; nonzero exit with GPU/OOM/CUDA-error signatures in stderr head -> candidate_crash; exit 0 but metric line missing/unparseable -> infra_crash (the eval contract itself is broken; per the fork's guidelines.md a stray line can also CREATE a false metric, so parse strictly: exactly one 'name: float' line matching the declared --metric); exit 124/137 or wall-clock >= T_max -> timeout (also infra-classified, since a hang is the eval's failure to terminate, though it may be candidate-caused - record the candidate anyway). (3) NULL SEMANTICS: candidate_crash -> value = crash sentinel = metric-floor imputation (0.0 for maximize, worst-observed*1.5 for minimize), crashed=true, campaign continues, candidate-failure counter++; infra_crash/timeout -> retry the SAME step once; on second failure infra_counter++, NO value recorded (field null, outcome recorded), step abandoned - never a fabricated number; any success resets infra_counter. (4) CIRCUIT BREAKER: halt the campaign with exit code 75 (distinct from 1) when infra_counter >= 3 consecutive OR infra share > 30% of the last 10 steps; K=1 stricter rule for the baseline canary below (SMAC abort_on_first_run_crash analog). (5) EVAL-HEALTH LANE: every 10 steps, re-evaluate the frozen baseline candidate; expected band from the window's median-of-N discipline; out-of-band -> infra failure + halt (this catches environment drift - clocks, thermals, driver - that rescales every metric silently, and catches a systematically-broken eval within 10 steps instead of overnight); embed 2-3 fixed canary oracle entries in every eval invocation (PASS_TO_PASS analog) - any canary miss marks that step's value invalid regardless of the printed metric. (6) POISON SCREENS: physical bounds from the runbook's derived floor/ceiling - out-of-bounds value is recorded but quarantined from champion promotion; implausible-jump rule - a claimed best beyond 5x the baseline's restart-variance band (bands 22-24% documented on this host) triggers a mandatory oracle re-run before promotion; eval script and oracle data live in a directory the mutator never edits. (7) MONITORING SURFACE: the ledger doubles as the health dashboard - null-rate, timeout-rate, wall-clock trend, baseline-band drift are first-class logged metrics with the runner's status line showing them live, so an overnight run's eval health is readable at a glance and a halted run's exit code says which breaker tripped.
failure_modes: How the pattern itself fails in the wild, with the known defense: (1) Timeout too tight culls legitimate slow candidates (AFL's classic mis-tuning) - calibrate T_max against the live wall-clock distribution, never a guess. (2) Crash-sentinel too extreme poisons the surrogate/model the optimizer builds (SMAC3's inf default is a documented annoyance; Vizier guidance says moderately negative, not extreme) - impute at the metric floor, not infinity. (3) Retry-once masks a systematic break if the breaker threshold is too high - 3-consecutive plus the 30%-over-10-steps window catches both bursts and slow leaks; the baseline canary catches the leak that never trips consecutive counters. (4) Signaling only the top-level process orphans GPU-holding children (GitHub Actions' documented behavior) - kill the process group, and verify GPU memory is freed before the next step starts. (5) The canary rots: the baseline band recorded under different clocks/thermals goes stale and either false-trips or false-passes - re-derive the band at window open (this host's preflight already does the known-good-control-first half). (6) Eval-health metrics become the gaming target if the optimizer can see or write them - keep the health lane, ledger, and eval script outside the candidate-writable surface (the SWE-bench lesson: harness applies ITS test patch over the candidate's). (7) Caching non-value outcomes as done (a null step never re-run) - SWE-bench's contract: only VALUE steps produce a 'done' artifact; unfinished ones are re-run on resume. (8) Silent grade inflation from empty or mis-parsed eval output ('no tests found' counting as pass; the fork's own 'correct: 0' comment-as-metric hazard) - strict single-metric-line parsing plus canary entries inside the eval. (9) Breaker false-trips on genuine GPU flake (this host documented 22-24% restart-variance bands) - the breaker counts INFRA-classified failures only, and bands used by the canary must be variance-aware, not point comparisons.
effort_estimate: Wrapper-level: everything above lands in tools/campaign-runner as a timeout+classify wrapper around the eval-command, a step-ledger JSONL, the breaker, and the baseline-canary lane - a few hundred lines of Python/shell around 'weco local run', no weco fork changes. Fork-level (optional, later): move retry semantics into the loop itself. Doctrine-only: the bounds/jump-rule/champion-quarantine rules go in the runbook (NEXT-WINDOW-RUNBOOK.md) as gates the operator already knows how to read.
priority_signal: FOR load-bearing: the exact named failure (a silently-broken eval burning an overnight campaign as nulls) is the cheapest defect to prevent and the most expensive to discover in wall-clock terms - every surveyed domain (SWE-bench, fuzzers, CI, AutoML) independently built the same three defenses, which is as close to convergent evolution as infrastructure practice gets; this host has already paid for the pattern once (probe driver abort-on-consecutive-failure, preflight known-good control) so the port is a proven-local idiom, not a new import; multi-day campaigns under median-of-N discipline make wall-clock the scarce resource a hung eval steals; and nothing else on the roadmap catches the hung case - oracle-first catches wrong values only. AGAINST / caveats: single-user host with a non-adversarial (clumsy, not strategic) mutator, so the poisoned-metric screens rank below the timeout/breaker in urgency; the fork already carries sandboxing (Quadlet/chroot), so isolation is not the gap; an over-tight breaker or point-comparison canary would false-halt on this host's documented 22-24% restart-variance bands - bands must be variance-aware. Priority order within the item: process-group timeout > three-valued outcome classification > circuit breaker (3 consecutive / 30% window) > baseline canary every N steps > poisoned-metric screens (bounds, jump rule, eval outside the mutation surface).
